A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perception-R1 work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–E support reliable comparison; the revision changes evaluation coverage without changing the work's identity.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and approach ablations, human perception-error analyses, training dynamics, and experiments with two model backbones in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds general-benchmark and vision-only evaluations, including results for both backbones and ablated variants.

M1.justification: The annotation extraction procedure, judging-LLM perception reward, format and accuracy rewards, repetition penalty, and GRPO optimization remain unchanged. The table label change from accuracy-only RLVR to GRPO does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MMStar, and EMMA, substantially broadening quantitative evaluation into multidisciplinary tasks beyond the four original math benchmarks. It also evaluates MMMU-Pro's vision-only input scenario. Geometry3K training and the original four benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds VLAA-Thinker and removes AtomThink, Kimi-k1.5, and InternVL3. R1-VL's previously reported MathVision comparison is omitted because of disclosed training overlap. MathVerse vision-only comparator membership also changes: Table 8 adds several reasoning baselines while dropping earlier URSA and Qwen2.5-VL-72B comparisons. Most principal comparators remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify MMMU val, MMMU-Pro overall and vision, MMStar val, and EMMA full settings. Tables 1 and 7 introduce exclusions for baseline results on benchmarks reportedly used in training. Existing math splits, greedy decoding, and training budgets remain unchanged; revised scores do not establish reruns or altered settings.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends component and SFT/reward-model ablations to general-domain performance. Appendix B.3 extends vision-only diagnostics to MMMU-Pro for both backbones. Conversely, earlier GEO/GPS and ablation-specific MathVerse vision-only breakdowns disappear. Sensitivity studies, human-error analyses, reward-hacking diagnostics, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same exact-binomial McNemar tests and one-sample t-test reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or another uncertainty-estimation practice. The tightened reported significance bound against Vision-R1 is a result-reporting change.

E6.justification: v2 adds many results, including Perception-R1 scores of 60.8, 41.4, 64.5, and 27.5 on MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MMStar, and EMMA. Its four overall math scores remain unchanged. Existing comparison scores change: R1-OneVision's MathVision result shifts from 29.9 to 21.9, reversing its ranking against Perception-R1's unchanged 28.6; SFT's WeMath score changes from 53.0 to 49.1. The reported Vision-R1 significance bound tightens from p < 0.05 to p < 0.01. These revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, assumptions underlying annotation construction, GRPO mathematics, and reward definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The introduction extends its explicit SOTA claim from math benchmarks to math and general benchmarks, and the abstract now emphasizes robustness. The central perception-bottleneck argument, reward-method contribution, data-efficiency claim, and conclusion remain substantively stable.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the main model's MathVision distribution-gap explanation with an interpretation of general-benchmark performance as evidence of robustness and transfer. New Appendix B.3 interprets expanded vision-only results as stronger perception evidence. Appendix E's annotation-reliability, judge-bias, and math-focused coverage limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes reported code and dataset availability from forthcoming to available. Training hyperparameters, hardware, training time, annotation construction details, and Appendix C prompts remain unchanged; external resource availability is not established by the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for VLAA-Thinker and the four general benchmarks, and removes the InternVL3 reference. AtomThink and Kimi remain cited despite their removal from Table 1. The main related-work discussion and methodological positioning are otherwise stable.

P1.justification: The title now foregrounds Perception-R1. The abstract, introduction, and evaluation discussion receive localized revisions, while Appendix B gains a vision-only subsection and subsequent subsections are renumbered. Main section order and most prose, including the method and conclusion, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 7 are substantially redesigned with math/general benchmark groups, split labels, and more compact formatting. GEO/GPS columns disappear; retained MathVerse vision-only results are reorganized into new Table 8 alongside additional comparisons. Existing figure content remains unchanged, with appendix page flow adjusted.

improvement.justification: General-domain evaluations of both backbones and ablations strengthen evidence for transfer beyond v1's math-focused quantitative tests. Training-overlap disclosures also improve comparison transparency. However, unexplained revisions to older scores and new table/prose inconsistencies limit the gain: v2 Table 2 reports SFT's EMMA score as 28.3 versus the base model's 24.9, contradicting the retained claim that SFT underperforms the base on every benchmark. The broader evidence therefore supports a limited net improvement.
